newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak crown seen extending gains in illiquid mkt.
newsitem.headline: Slovak crown seen extending gains in illiquid mkt.

text.p: The Slovak crown gained around 160 basis points in thin Thursday morning trading and dealers said the currency was likely to strengthen further during the day.
At 0800 GMT the crown was at around -3.0 percent on the depreciation side of parity with its mark/dollar basket, firming from around -4.6 percent at the open of trading.
"The crown firmed immediately after the market opened today, but it remains volatile as banks are still quoting low volumes and wide spreads," said Tibor Fratrik of ING Bank.
Another Bratislava-based trader said foreign traders were willing to buy crowns at levels close to its band floor of -7.0 percent.
But Fratrik said it was hard to track the crown's market price since both the Slovak foreign exchange and money markets were highly illiquid at the moment.
"It is hard to talk about a real crown price, we will have to wait until the FX and money markets return to normal, more liquid trading," he added.
The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has deliberately kept the crown money market short of liquidity to prevent speculators from obtaining funds which could be used for short-selling.

The NBS said it would not hold a repo tender on Thursday to further keep the market illiquid. According to NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector lacked 6.17 percent of required funds to meet its minimum reserves requirement on Friday.
"The market appears to believe that the crown will not weaken beyond its band floor and we think the NBS fixing will even support this attitude," said one local trader.

He said the NBS appeared committed to keep supporting the crown by fixing it stronger than market levels and that the crown market price would probably approach the central bank fixing rate in the near future.
"The NBS seems strong enough to keep strong crown fixing, so the market will have to adjust to it and the crown will then strengthen," he said.

The NBS on Wednesday, for the seventh consecutive day, fixed the Slovak crown above market levels, at 33.316 to the dollar and at 19.542 to the mark, implying a deviation of -0.67 percent versus the basket parity.
